note: Satellite crops (Esri World Imagery, z18) of the top flagged crash corridors. OSM records no lane or width tag on these roads, so the design-speed proxy leans on class and alignment; the satellite is the physical evidence that closes the gap. Lane counts are read by eye against the 25 m scale bar on each crop and hand-verified, not auto-measured (an automated grey-pixel transect was tried and discarded as unreliable over medians, elevated rail, and water). Width in metres is deliberately not asserted per road; the image plus scale bar is the evidence.

featured.read: A ten-plus lane megahighway with side service roads, bumper to bumper in the daytime image. The jam is the crawl a skeptic points to; the road is built as a speedway. When it clears at night, the crash you have is twice as likely to injure or kill.
A dead-straight arterial under the LRT-1 line, cutting through wall-to-wall housing on both sides. Straight and wide invites speed the moment it clears.
A straight arterial slicing through Cebu's dense core, homes and a church right at the kerb.
A new, wide, divided coastal highway running directly past dense informal housing. Built new for speed, next to people on foot.
